newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Threat to Bosnian gas supply over payment.
newsitem.headline: Threat to Bosnian gas supply over payment.

text.p: A dispute between Bosnian Serbs and the Moslem-Croat federation on how a $12.4 million debt for imported natural gas supply should be divided could cause a cut in supplies next week, western officials said on Friday.

Colum Murphy, spokesman for the international community's representative in Bosnia Carl Bildt, said that a conditional agreement had been reached with Russia's Gas Export to pay the bill by February 15.
"Now the gas bill still has not been paid and the suppliers are beginning to further ration the gas supply," Murphy told reporters.
The Sarajevo media reported that Gas Export notified the Bosnian gas import company on Thursday it would reduce the amount of gas to Bosnia from next Monday.

A federation official said agreement was reached between Bosnian Serb part of the country and the federation how to pay about half of the debt, but differences remained unsolved regarding the other half.
The gas reduction would have a devastating effect on elderly and those who cannot afford to pay electric heating, Murphy said.
